record.context_brief: MSF wavelets vs existence of wavelets
record.original_question:
Fix (A,Γ) with A ∈ GL_n(R) and Γ ⊂ R^n a full rank lattice. Suppose an orthonormal wavelet associated with (A,Γ) exists.

Must there also exist a minimally supported frequency (MSF) wavelet associated with (A,Γ), where MSF means |ψ̂| = 1_W for some measurable set W that is a wavelet set (tiles by translations and dilations, modulo null sets)?

evidence.quote:
The expectation is that the answers to Problems 3.1 and 3.2 are actually the same. In
other words, if there exists an o.n. wavelet associated with (A, Γ), then there also exists
an MSF wavelet associated with (A, Γ). However, this is unknown since even more basic
problem involving Calderón’s formula remains open.

Equivalently, ψ ∈ L2 (R) is an MSF wavelet if and only if |ψ̂| = 1W for some measurable
set W ⊂ R, known as wavelet set, which satisfies simultaneous translation and dilation tiling
of R. That is,
     • {W + k}k∈Z is a partition of R modulo null sets, and
     • {2j W }j∈Z is a partition of R modulo null sets.

Definition 3.2. Let (A, Γ) be a dilation-lattice pair. We say that W ⊂ Rn is an (A, Γ)-
wavelet set if
   (t) {W + γ}k∈Γ is a partition of Rn modulo null sets, and
   (d) {Aj W }j∈Z is a partition of Rn modulo null sets.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n\ge 1$. Fix an invertible matrix $A\in\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{R})$ and a full-rank lattice $\Gamma\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ (i.e., $\Gamma = P\mathbb{Z}^n$ for some $P\in\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{R})$). A finite collection $\Psi=\{\psi^1,\ldots,\psi^L\}\subset L^2(\mathbb{R}^n)$ is called an orthonormal wavelet associated with $(A,\Gamma)$ if the system
$$\{|\det A|^{j/2}\,\psi^\ell(A^j x-\gamma) : j\in\mathbb{Z},\ \gamma\in\Gamma,\ \ell=1,\ldots,L\}$$
is an orthonormal basis of $L^2(\mathbb{R}^n)$. (We restrict to the case $L=1$ of single-generator orthonormal wavelets.)

A measurable set $W\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ is called an $(A,\Gamma)$-wavelet set if
\begin{itemize}
\item[(t)] $\{W+\gamma\}_{\gamma\in\Gamma^*}$ partitions $\mathbb{R}^n$ modulo null sets, where $\Gamma^*$ is the dual lattice, and
\item[(d)] $\{(A^T)^j W\}_{j\in\mathbb{Z}}$ partitions $\mathbb{R}^n$ modulo null sets.
\end{itemize}
A function $\psi\in L^2(\mathbb{R}^n)$ is called a minimally supported frequency (MSF) wavelet associated with $(A,\Gamma)$ if $|\widehat{\psi}|=\mathbf{1}_W$ (up to normalization) for some $(A,\Gamma)$-wavelet set $W$; equivalently, $\psi$ is an orthonormal wavelet whose Fourier transform has minimal possible support.

Question: Suppose there exists a single-generator orthonormal wavelet associated with $(A,\Gamma)$. Must there exist a minimally supported frequency wavelet associated with $(A,\Gamma)$?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of whether existence of an orthonormal wavelet for a dilation-lattice pair $(A,\Gamma)$ implies existence of an MSF wavelet for $(A,\Gamma)$ is listed among open problems in wavelet theory. Even the more basic question characterizing dilations admitting MSF wavelets is fully resolved only in dimension $n=2$ (Ionascu–Wang following Speegle); higher-dimensional cases and the equivalence between the two existence problems remain open.

status_evidence.title: Open Problems in Wavelet Theory (M. Bownik)
status_evidence.snippet: The expectation is that the answers to Problems 3.1 and 3.2 are actually the same... However, this is unknown since even more basic problem involving Calderón's formula remains open.
status_evidence.claim: The implication 'existence of an orthonormal wavelet for (A,Γ) ⇒ existence of an MSF wavelet for (A,Γ)' is stated as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Wavelets for Non-expanding Dilations and the Lattice Counting Estimate
status_evidence.snippet: Ionascu and Wang proved a complete characterization of dilations admitting MSF wavelet in dimension n=2, while the corresponding problem in higher dimensions n ≥ 3 remains open.
status_evidence.claim: Characterization of dilations admitting MSF wavelets remains open in dimensions n≥3.
